source_documents.title: Facile Synthesis of Dicyclohepta[ cd , fg ]‐ as ‐indacene and Confirmation of its Anti‐Kasha S 3 Emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: Compound 1-Ph-Me exhibits near-infrared (NIR) absorption as well as weak anti-Kasha emission.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-Ph-Me

reference_evidence_units.quote: Notably, two absorption bands ranging from 750 to 1700 nm (S0 → S1 band) and 520 to 680 nm (S0 → S2 band) showed no overlap with the excitation spectrum, indicating that the observed emission originates from the S3 excited state of 1-Ph-Me (Figure S18).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-Ph-Me

reference_evidence_units.quote: In this sense, the S0 → S2 transition of azulene, which potentially decays with emission, almost corresponds to the S0 → S3 and S0 → S4 transitions of 1-Ph-Me (shown in red).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-Ph-Me
reference_evidence_units.statement: The emissive azulene-like state is S3 in the dimer: the state order of the fused biazulene explains which state emits.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The loose-bolt effect associated with the phenyl groups is also likely to contribute [38].
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-Ph-Me
reference_evidence_units.statement: Phenyl motion may shorten the emission lifetime.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, 1-Ph-Me displayed an anti-Kasha emission peak at 616 nm, representing a six-fold enhancement compared to 1-Ph, although the under lying mechanism is not yet fully understood.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-Ph-Me vs 1-Ph
reference_evidence_units.statement: Methyl groups raise the S3 emission six-fold, mechanism unknown.
